subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the tangent and normal at the positive end of the latus rectum on the parabola y² = 6x.

mark_split.label: Find a and the positive end of the latus rectum

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Maths-2B, book p.83 — VSAQ chapter 14 Parabola, answer 128. No appearance tag is printed. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, same page-format reasoning as the rest of this chapter. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and the positive end of the latus rectum
steps.margin_note: First mark, for a = 3/2 and the point (3/2, 3).
lines: The positive end of the latus rectum is (a, 2a) = (3/2, 3)
steps.why: The latus rectum is the chord through the focus perpendicular to the axis, and its two ends are always (a,2a) and (a,−2a) — the positive end is the one with the positive y-coordinate.
common_mistakes: Writing the latus rectum's end as (2a, a) with the coordinates swapped.
Using the negative end (a, −2a) instead of the positive one asked for.
steps.memory_tip: The latus rectum's ends are always (a, 2a) and (a, −2a) — same x-coordinate as the focus, y equal to ±2a.

steps.label: Write the tangent and normal
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for both the tangent and the normal — this question asks for two equations, not one.
lines: Tangent at (x₁,y₁) on y² = 4ax is yy₁ = 2a(x + x₁): y(3) = 3(x + 3/2) ⇒ y = x + 3/2 ⇒ 2x − 2y + 3 = 0
Slope of this tangent is 1, so the slope of the normal is −1
steps.why: The tangent comes straight from the standard point-form of the tangent formula, and the normal follows immediately once the tangent's slope is known, since a normal is always perpendicular to its tangent.
common_mistakes: Using the normal's slope formula directly instead of first finding the tangent's slope and flipping its sign.
Making an arithmetic slip converting y − 3 = −1(x − 3/2) into the final whole-number form.
steps.memory_tip: Find the tangent first — its slope, flipped in sign, is the normal's slope, since a normal is always perpendicular to its tangent.

insider_note: Two full equations are expected for two marks — writing only the tangent, or only the normal, earns half credit at best.
